scope.frame: the harmonic level surfaces of B1846's harmonic time, read by their own conformal modulus
scope.object: m004 (LR) around its whole circle; the excursion member L^6 R L R at s = 1/4 and s = 1/2 (the anti-apex); its tube level s = 0 NOT computed
scope.hypotheses: data-free; the modulus from three Dirichlet energies (det E = 1 as the check); two meshing methods; tau reduced to the standard fundamental domain

claim_one_line: THE LEVEL SURFACE'S OWN MODULUS (P-727; data-free): an instrument reading the conformal modulus of a harmonic level surface from its 3D shape and its fibre group alone -- validated on a Fuchsian control of known tau (recovered to < 2e-4 after Richardson; second order; a curved 3D-inverted copy agrees) -- gives the metric's own, fourth reading of the fibre's shape. On m004 the loop is forced at its symmetric levels (s = 0, 1/2: -1/2 + 1.12438i; s = 1/4, 3/4: i) and closes; it sits 0.57% above the golden Teichmuller apex 1/2 + (sqrt5/2)i. On the excursion member L^6RLR: the anti-apex s = 1/2 reads 1/2 + 1.5904i (Re 1/2 forced), 16% above the Teichmuller anti-apex 1/2 + sqrt(15/8) i; s = 1/4 reads -0.3722 + 1.0085i by two independent meshings. The tube level s = 0 is NOT computed: the surface folds there (a helicoid about the tube's core, which lies on a face of the fibre group's fundamental piece) and both instruments fail their own checks -- P-727 stays open for that value. 0 of 19.
